what_changed: base year: constant-price series are on 2015=100. The catalogue's real GDP files start in 2015 for that reason; the long real GDP & GNI series (gdp_gni_annual_real, from 1970) is spliced across earlier base years by the source.
source_note: DOSM, gdp_annual_real_supply catalogue entry (no single bullet; see methodology_en)

what_changed: poverty line redefined (PLI revised with the 2019 HIES). The absolute-poverty headcount steps from 0.4% in 2016 to 5.6% in 2019 and hardcore poverty from 0.0% to 0.4%, while median household income ROSE +12.3% over the same interval — the step is the poverty line moving, not household welfare. Pre-2019 and 2019-onward absolute and hardcore poverty are NOT one series and must not be differenced. Relative poverty (below half the national median) is defined independently of the PLI and runs from 1995.
source_note: DOSM, hh_poverty methodology_en: 'For full details on the methodology, especially the computation of the PLI and its evolution and nuances, please refer to the technical notes' — https://open.dosm.gov.my/publications/technical-notes/hies-technotes. Step sizes above are computed from the ingested hh_poverty.csv / hh_income.csv.

what_changed: nominal, not real: every HIES income figure is in current prices and is NOT deflated. Comparing 1970 to 2024 income without applying cpi_headline measures inflation, not welfare.
source_note: DOSM, hh_income caveat_en: 'This data presents nominal values, i.e. they have not been adjusted for inflation.'

what_changed: the percentile files carry materially larger relative standard errors than the headline mean/median, by construction. Treat single-percentile movements as noise unless corroborated.
source_note: DOSM, hies_malaysia_percentile caveat_en: 'This data should be used with caution as the relative standard errors are larger due to the higher resolution.'

what_changed: missing years: 1991 and 1994 are absent from the annual LFS series entirely (sample limitations), so an unbroken annual line through those years is interpolation, not data.
source_note: DOSM, lfs_year caveat_en: 'Data for 1991 and 1994 are not available due to limitations in the sample data from those years.'

what_changed: seasonally adjusted series are adjusted series-by-series (X-12-ARIMA + SEAM), so their components do NOT add to their totals. Verified: median |lf - (employed + unemployed)| in lfs_month_sa is 4.5 thousand. Use the unadjusted files for levels and any accounting identity.
source_note: DOSM, gdp_qtr_real_sa methodology_en: 'Seasonal adjustment was conducted using X-12-ARIMA, augmented with the Seasonal Adjustment for Malaysia (SEAM) procedure'; verified in data/_validation_realeconomy.csv

what_changed: open vintages: the most recent years are provisional and are revised at the next release — GDP states 2024 and 2025 may be revised, the SA series names 2022-2024, productivity names the most recent 3 years, IPI the most recent 1 year, BOP and FDI the most recent 8 quarters, and trade the most recent 2 months. Any level taken from those windows is a moving target; _vintage.json pins which one we hold.
source_note: DOSM, gdp_annual_nominal_supply caveat_en: 'Values for 2024 and 2025 may be revised in future releases.'

what_changed: the 2024 wave was published mid-ingest and revised 2022 as well as adding 2024: the file first retrieved ended at 2022, and within the same session the storage CSV moved to the 2024 wave with the overlapping 2022 values changed. The warehouse holds the 2024-wave file. Anyone holding an earlier copy of this dataset has different 2022 numbers — the reason every DOSM file here is vintage-pinned in data/_vintage.json rather than assumed stable.
source_note: observed 2026-08-03 by pipeline/verify_realeconomy.py (parquet and API mirrors carried 2024 before the CSV did) and confirmed by pipeline/refresh.py detecting the new vintage (data_as_of 2022 -> 2024)

what_changed: ep_ratio is not comparable across LFS datasets: lfs_year's ep_ratio reproduces 100*employed/(lf+outside) exactly, but lfs_year_sex and lfs_state_sex publish a different ep_ratio for identical labour-force levels in the same year (e.g. 1982: 62.7 vs 62.5; 2008: 60.6 vs 58.1). Join ep_ratio from one dataset only.
source_note: observed 2026-08-03 by pipeline/verify_realeconomy.py; 1,464 of 1,732 lfs_state_sex rows breach the identity, median 1.38pp, max 45pp — see data/_identity_breaches_realeconomy.csv

what_changed: small-area cells that do not add up: at district/parliament/DUN grain some published rows have lf != employed + unemployed by far more than rounding (lfs_dun max 109.7 thousand at Johor N.49 Kota Iskandar 2023; lfs_district Sabah/Tongod 2020 prints lf=83.0 between 22.8 in 2019 and 14.9 in 2021, and its p_rate/ep_ratio are computed from that outlier). Kept as published; do not aggregate small-area LFS cells to a state or national total.
source_note: observed 2026-08-03 by pipeline/verify_realeconomy.py; every breaching row listed in data/_identity_breaches_realeconomy.csv

what_changed: the 2022 percentile distribution does not average back to the published 2022 mean: mean of the 100 percentile means is RM 8,359.7 against a published mean of RM 8,479 (-1.4%). The 2019 and 2024 waves reconcile to within 0.03%. Use the headline mean for 2022 levels and the percentile file for shape only.
